passage: Abstract: "A frequent experimental flaw is the application of oversampling algorithms to the entire dataset, resulting in biased models and overly-optimistic estimates." (copying rows = random oversampling, L1.4 by PB's tie rule, SOURCES_D)
faulty: Random oversampling (minority rows copied with replacement until classes have equal counts) is applied to all 1000 records; stratified 10-fold cross-validation with a 5-nearest-neighbour classifier (probability = share of positive neighbours) then runs on the enlarged data; the AUC of the pooled test-fold scores is the statistic. Claim holds when AUC >= 0.75.
fixed: Stratified 10-fold cross-validation on the original records; oversampling of the training folds only; AUC on the original test-fold records, pooled.
estimand: Faulty: AUC on test rows that are copies of training rows. Fixed: AUC on new records.
model_family: 5-nearest-neighbour classifier with random oversampling. Chosen by me: the abstract names no classifier; duplicates are their own nearest neighbours.
sizes_note: Source sizes: not stated in the abstract (full text not open). 1000 x 15 = 15k values, a mid-size regime; cheap. Dependence on imbalance: not stated.
exploited_structure: A small event class whose rows are repeated, so a test copy has its twin in the fitting data.

structure_statistic.note_value_source: source states none: the abstract gives no imbalance ratio; 9.0 (a 90/10 split) is proposed as typical

notes: Reserve for SAN18 L1.4. Differs from B2B-05 in statistic (AUC vs sensitivity), size (1000 x 15 vs 400 x 8) and model.
